notes: Copy a fixture into a fresh temp directory, `git init` it with one commit, then run the prompt there. The prompts pre-answer the interview so a run can finish unattended; a separate check (interview-only) confirms the interview itself.

evals.name: light-preset-small-script
evals.prompt: Set this repo up for agents. I'm the only one working on it, sessions run only on my laptop, and I use Claude Code. Take your recommendations without asking me again.
evals.expected_output: Light preset. AGENTS.md plus a CLAUDE.md pointer; BACKLOG.md; a best-effort format-on-edit hook using ruff; workflow and maintenance folded into AGENTS.md; .agentic/config.json with preset light.
expectations: AGENTS.md exists, is under ~60 lines, and names the run command for rename_photos.py
CLAUDE.md exists and imports AGENTS.md instead of repeating its rules
No docs/decisions/, docs/plans/, .agentic/scripts/, .githooks/pre-push or review-loop skill was created
The format-on-edit hook exits 0 when ruff is not installed
.agentic/config.json is valid JSON with preset 'light'
The final report lists the modules skipped and why

evals.name: standard-retrofit-respects-existing-practice
evals.prompt: Retrofit the agentic workflow onto this repo. We're a team of three on Claude Code and Codex, and some sessions run in Claude Code on the web. Use the Standard preset and the review loop; don't install any third-party tools. Take your other recommendations without asking me again.
evals.expected_output: Standard preset. CLAUDE.md content moved into AGENTS.md (the money and testing rules kept, the 'Current status' section dropped and mentioned in the report); GitHub Issues kept as the backlog, no BACKLOG.md; the existing husky pre-commit extended rather than replaced; review kit installed under .agentic/ with the pre-push hook chained through husky or .githooks; branch prefixes for both agents; cloud SessionStart hooks; decision 0001 recording the scaffold.
expectations: AGENTS.md contains the 'integer cents' rule and the 'every endpoint has a test' rule
No file contains 'Working on the PDF export this sprint'; the report mentions dropping the status section
CLAUDE.md is a pointer to AGENTS.md
There is no BACKLOG.md; AGENTS.md says work is in GitHub Issues with the 'ready' label
.husky/pre-commit still runs prettier
.agentic/config.json lists agentBranchPrefixes for both claude and codex
`node --test .agentic/scripts/*.test.mjs` passes
The hook entry (.husky/pre-push) and .agentic/scripts/pre-push.sh are mode 100755 in the index, and pre-push.sh has no '{{AGENT_BRANCH_PREFIXES}}' placeholder
package.json has a `prepare` script that runs husky, and .agentic/config.json records hookManager 'husky'
.agents/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md exists, and .claude/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md only points to it
.claude/settings.json has SessionStart hooks that install dependencies only when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is true, and set core.hooksPath
docs/decisions/0001-*.md records the preset, modules and the kept divergences
No seeds, mulch, no-mistakes or treehouse files or commands were added

evals.name: full-preset-monorepo
evals.prompt: Scaffold the full agentic workflow here. Two of us run several Claude Code sessions in parallel locally; nothing runs in the cloud. Use the CI check for the gate. Don't install treehouse; use plain git worktrees. Take your other recommendations without asking me again.
evals.expected_output: Full preset. Root AGENTS.md extended (not replaced) plus one AGENTS.md per package; plan template with per-step boundaries; review kit plus .github/workflows/review-loop-check.yml; parallel-sessions section using git worktree without treehouse; no cloud hooks.
expectations: The root AGENTS.md still says 'The acme product: an API and a web app.'
packages/api/AGENTS.md and packages/web/AGENTS.md exist and only cover their package
docs/plans/TEMPLATE.md has acceptance criteria and a 'Stop and ask if' line per step
.github/workflows/review-loop-check.yml checks out the base sha, not the head
The workflow doc describes parallel sessions with git worktree and does not install treehouse
The workflow doc says a branch must be renamed to an agent prefix before pushing, with the command
.claude/settings.json has no SessionStart dependency-install hook, but does have one that turns hooks on
packages/api/CLAUDE.md and packages/web/CLAUDE.md point to their AGENTS.md
`node .agentic/scripts/gate-selftest.mjs` passes

evals.name: standard-python-pre-commit-framework
evals.prompt: Set this repo up for agents with the Standard preset and the review loop. I use Claude Code, locally only. Don't install any third-party tools. Take your other recommendations without asking me again.
evals.expected_output: Standard preset. The existing pre-commit framework is kept as the hook manager: a local pre-push hook is added to .pre-commit-config.yaml that runs loop-gate.mjs --pre-commit; the ruff hooks stay. No .githooks/ or .husky/ entry. .pre-commit-config.yaml gains default_install_hook_types for both stages, so the README's existing `pre-commit install` turns the gate on. Review kit under .agentic/.
expectations: .pre-commit-config.yaml keeps the ruff hooks and gains a local pre-push hook running `node .agentic/scripts/loop-gate.mjs --pre-commit`
.agentic/config.json records hookManager 'pre-commit'
No .githooks/pre-push or .husky/pre-push was created
.agentic/scripts/pre-push.sh is mode 100755 and has its prefixes filled in
AGENTS.md tells a new clone to run `pre-commit install`, and .pre-commit-config.yaml has default_install_hook_types covering pre-push
`node --test .agentic/scripts/*.test.mjs` passes
The report notes that pytest/ruff could not be run if dependencies were not installed, as pre-existing

evals.name: interview-only
evals.prompt: Set this repo up for agents.
evals.expected_output: No files written. One message: what was detected, a recommended preset, settings with recommended values, a file plan, and a question asking whether to go ahead. Asks whether sessions run in the cloud.
expectations: No files in the repo were created or modified
The message recommends a preset and gives a reason
The message proposes keeping GitHub Issues and the husky hook
The message asks where sessions run (local, cloud, or both)
Any third-party tool mentioned comes with what it installs and whether it sends telemetry
